sections.h2: What is Multnomah County, Oregon, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Multnomah County is the smallest county in Oregon by area, at 466 square miles, and it holds Portland, the county seat and largest city. It lies on the south side of the Columbia River, the Willamette River runs through it, and the Boring Lava Field's extinct volcanoes are part of the landscape.

The county was created on December 22, 1854, as the 13th county in Oregon Territory, carved from Washington and Clackamas counties after Portland businessmen petitioned for it. The name comes from a Chinookan word for the lower river. The 2020 census counted 815,428 residents.

ItemMultnomah County fact
Total area466 square miles, 34 of them water

Other citiesGresham, Troutdale, Fairview, Wood Village, Maywood Park

Portland itself is split into six addressing sectors (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW), with the Willamette dividing east from west and Burnside Street dividing north from south. A listing that says "SE" or "NE" is telling you the side of the river and the side of Burnside before you read anything else.

sections.h2: What do Multnomah County jobs and employers mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Trade, transportation and utilities lead the county, followed by private education and health services, professional and business services, and government. Wikipedia's 2024 figures put total nonfarm employment at about 510,000, with roughly 93,200 in trade, transportation and utilities and 81,200 in government.

Employers on the 2024 Portland list include Intel at about 23,200 workers, Oregon Health & Science University at about 20,900, Providence Health & Services at about 20,700, Kaiser Foundation at about 13,100 and Nike at about 10,700. Marine terminals at the port handle more than 13 million tons of cargo a year.

Two things follow for a house seller:

  • A seller moving for a job at one of these employers may need a fixed closing date, which is hard to promise on a house needing repairs.
  • Oregon has no sales tax, which draws shoppers from southwest Washington but has no effect on what a property owner pays in property tax.

sections.h2: How do Portland weather, landslides and older housing affect a sale?
sections.html:
Portland winters are cool, cloudy and wet, with about 37 inches of precipitation a year on roughly 157 rainy days. Freezing temperatures show up on about 32 nights a year, snow averages about 4 inches, and summers are dry, with 80 degrees or more on about 61 days. The record high of 116 degrees was set on June 28, 2021.

A 2014 report flagged more than 7,000 locations in Portland as high risk for landslides and soil liquefaction in a major earthquake, including much of the west side. Hillside lots can raise questions about retaining walls, drainage and insurance that a buyer's lender may want answered.

Older houses and wet winters make roofs, drainage and foundations the usual inspection topics. Selling as-is can avoid a repair negotiation, but it does not remove the need to disclose what you know.

Portland ended single-family-only zoning in 2021, so a larger lot may also be worth a conversation about what else could be built on it.

sections.h2: When are Multnomah County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The 2026 due date is Monday, November 16, because November 15 falls on a Sunday. Bills are mailed by October 25, and the county sent about 300,000 statements and value notices this year.

ChoicePaymentsDiscount
Full paymentNovember 16, 20263 percent
Two-thirdsNovember 16, 2026, then May 17, 20272 percent
Three equal paymentsNov. 16, 2026; Feb. 16, 2027; May 17, 2027None

Taxes under $40 must be paid in full on the November date. Past-due balances carry interest of 1.3333 percent per month, which is 16 percent a year, and a returned check costs $25. The county says it does not have the legal authority to extend the deadline or waive interest.

You can pay online, by phone at 503-988-2225, by mail to P.O. Box 2716, Portland, OR 97208-2716, in person at Suite 175, or in the 24-hour drop box for checks at 501 SE Hawthorne. Total property taxes and special assessments countywide for 2026 are $2.602 billion, about 3.5 percent above 2025.

sections.h2: How do Multnomah County values and the tax limits work?
sections.html:
Your bill starts from real market value, the assessor's estimate as of January 1, and uses assessed value, which is the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value. Growth in assessed value on existing property is limited to 3 percent a year under Measure 50.

Measure 5 separately caps operating taxes at $5 per $1,000 of real market value for schools and $10 per $1,000 for general government. The county's statement guide says the difference between the Measure 5 and Measure 50 calculations is called compression, and you can see a property's compression history in the county's TaxGraph tool.

  • Education, general government and bond taxes appear on separate lines for each district.
  • Renovations made by January 1 can raise the value on the next statement.
  • A yellow statement means a mortgage company or deferral program asked for the bill.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Multnomah County value, and what will the board refuse to hear?
sections.html:
File a petition with the county's Property Values Appeals Board postmarked or delivered by December 31. The board is a panel of private citizens appointed by the county commissioners and is separate from the assessor's office.

  1. Choose the right form: real property, personal property or late-filing penalty.
  2. Pay $30 per account to Multnomah County.
  3. Mail to PO Box 5007, Portland, OR 97208-5007, or deliver to 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd, Suite 175. Email and fax are not accepted, and a postage meter imprint does not count as a postmark.
  4. Wait for a notice, mailed 5 to 10 days before a hearing. Hearings run from February through April 15.
  5. Present your case in about 5 minutes, and expect a decision the same day.

Useful evidence is an arm's-length sale or a fee appraisal near January 1, comparable sales, written repair estimates or contractor costs. The board cannot reduce the 3 percent increase over the prior year's assessed value, except for an exception such as new improvements. It also cannot weigh hardship or hear arguments about tax rates. A written order usually arrives within a week, and further appeals go to the Oregon Tax Court.

sections.h2: What happens if you fall behind on Multnomah County property tax?
sections.html:
Taxes become a lien on July 1, and real property can be foreclosed once three years have passed since the earliest delinquency. In the county's example, 2021 taxes became delinquent on May 16, 2022, and the property became subject to foreclosure in May 2025.

  • Interest builds at 1.3333 percent a month after the 15th of each month.
  • Any payment is applied to the oldest tax owed.
  • Foreclosure notices are mailed to the owner and explain the payment timeline.
  • For business property the county uses a Notice of Intent to Warrant, then a recorded warrant, which can lead to garnishment or seizure.

A payment plan can help avoid escalated collection. Ask for eligibility through the online request form or by calling Tax Collections at 503-988-3334. If you owe several years, it is worth getting advice early, because the three-year clock runs from the earliest unpaid year.

sections.h2: How do deeds get recorded in Multnomah County when a house sells?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Multnomah County Recorder, part of the Division of Assessment, Recording and Taxation. Most sales are recorded through the title company by eRecording, with submissions closing at 4:15 p.m. each day.

You can also mail documents to PO Box 5007, use the 24-hour drop box at the Multnomah Building, or walk in at 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd, Suite 175, between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Since January 1, 2024, recorded documents must use at least 10-point type. The office cannot give legal advice or help fill in forms, and it returns a document with an explanation if it cannot be recorded as presented.

Before closing, give the title company the latest statement and any lien notices. This guide is general information, so confirm details with the county office.

faqs.q: When is the Multnomah County property tax due in 2026?
faqs.a: November 16, 2026, because November 15 is a Sunday. Pay in full for a 3 percent discount or two-thirds for 2 percent, or pay three equal installments with no discount.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to appeal a Multnomah County property value?
faqs.a: The filing fee is $30 per account, payable to Multnomah County. The petition must be postmarked or delivered by December 31, and email or fax filings are not accepted.

faqs.q: What interest does Multnomah County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is 1.3333 percent per month, or 16 percent a year, on past-due amounts. The county says it cannot waive interest or extend the due date.

faqs.q: When can Multnomah County foreclose on unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Real property becomes subject to foreclosure after three years from the earliest delinquency. A payment plan may help owners avoid escalated collection.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Multnomah County house with taxes still owed?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the owed taxes and interest are paid at closing from the sale proceeds. Because payments go to the oldest tax year first, ask the county for a payoff figure and share it with the title company.
